In the Data For Good generative AI white paper, BLOOM's estimated training carbon footprint initially was calculated at 30 tonnes CO2eq based on direct energy consumption (433 MWh) and the carbon intensity of the electricity used (57 g CO2eq/kWh). 

When extending the scope to include additional factors such as the consumption of other essential data center equipment (switches, routers, storage servers), the energy consumption estimate increased from 433 MWh to 690 MWh, raising the impact to 39.3 tonnes CO2eq (without considering PUE separately).

Further including the environmental impact of manufacturing the servers and GPUs used for training (considering a 6-year lifespan and estimated manufacturing emissions of 3,700 kg CO2eq per server and 150 kg CO2eq per GPU), the impact rose to 50.5 tonnes CO2eq.

Finally, when adding the phase of model development (which includes multiple tests, evaluations, and corrections during training), an additional 73.32 tonnes CO2eq was added. This brought the total full-scope estimate of BLOOM's carbon footprint to 123.82 tonnes CO2eq.

Thus, BLOOM's estimated training carbon footprint increased from the initial 30 tonnes CO2eq to a full-scope estimate of approximately 124 tonnes CO2eq, which is about four times higher than the initial calculation.
